justification: Critical: changes the flood verdict served on the flood tool, the PDF and the Site Report. 144 of 308 saved checks move down a level.

pre_impl.existing_data: copernicus_flood_events EMSR567 = one row of 86,349 km2 (5 polygons); the ingest merged every shapefile in each ZIP, including area-of-interest layers. property_reports: 308 latest flood checks, 144 at moderate or above with EMS (alone or with a water trace under 15%) the only positive.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: EMS was treated as an observed flood extent; EMSR567 is a whole mapped region, so a hit says nothing about the lot.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Edits the single rule every surface reads (_compute_flood_signal); the PDF and Site Report take flood_signal from it, so no surface computes its own verdict.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No new external call. EMS lookup failure already returns None, which never counted.
pre_impl.frontend_type: flood_signal values unchanged in type: one of none/low/moderate/elevated/unavailable.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A lot that truly flooded and is covered only by EMS now shows no signal; mitigated because the real 2022 extents in the fixture also carry council/study positives and stay elevated.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: EMS alone can still decide a level, or any saved check moves up a level
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before the fix the same command printed EMS_ONLY_POSITIVE=144; after it prints EMS_ONLY_POSITIVE=0 RAISED=0 LOWERED=144 UNCHANGED=164.

functions.name: _compute_flood_signal
functions.input: the normalised flood outputs dict for one lot, from every queried source
functions.output: one of none, low, moderate, elevated or unavailable
functions.if_none: missing inputs count as negative; EPI query failure returns unavailable

break_it.scenario: A lot that really flooded in 2022 is covered only by an EMS extent
break_it.what_happens: The page now shows that lot with no flood signal at all, although it flooded
break_it.how: Accepted until EMSR567 is re-ingested with flood-extent layers only (next step); the three real-extent fixture cases also carry council or study positives and stay elevated

break_it.scenario: The fix accidentally raises a lot that had no flood signal
break_it.what_happens: A lot with no flood evidence would get a new and false flood warning
break_it.how: Regression gate requires RAISED=0 over all 308 saved checks

break_it.scenario: Real flood evidence is lost along with EMS
break_it.what_happens: Council flood planning areas or overlay lots would drop to showing no signal
break_it.how: Known-answer positives still pass with EMS ignored entirely (mutation check: 13 passed)
break_it.repro: set ems_detected = False and run the known-answer tests

break_it.scenario: An old saved result is served from the cache after the fix
break_it.what_happens: A customer re-opening an older check could still see the old moderate verdict
break_it.how: flood_signal is never stored; it is recomputed from saved inputs on every read, so cached checks get the new rule
break_it.repro: SELECT count(*) FROM property_reports WHERE product='flood' AND outputs ? 'flood_signal' returns 0

break_it.scenario: An EMS-only lot with no local flood study now reads as clear
break_it.what_happens: An absence of flood data could be read by the owner as no flood risk
break_it.how: Lots with no council study and no water history still return unavailable; lots where the council was queried return none. The page wording for none is fixed in the next page PR

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - re-run scripts/run_flood_calibration_2022.py and correct the published recall in docs/qa/flood-calibration-2022-result.md before quoting any accuracy figure
